Short recommendation
- Keep a single legal Company for tax reporting, and model each outlet as an Organization (department/branch) so you can track profitability and cash per store while keeping consolidated tax books at the Company level [doc:applications/accounting/src/docs/asciidoc/_include/acc-intro.adoc-0][7766061-14].
- Use the Global Chart of Accounts master template as the source of truth. Create any new accounts you need (for store P&L, store cash, inter‑org transfer clearing, etc.) in the Global chart, then assign only the accounts each Organization will actively use to that Organization’s Chart of Accounts [doc:applications/accounting/src/docs/asciidoc/_include/HELP_ListGlAccountOrganization.adoc-0][doc:applications/accounting/src/docs/asciidoc/_include/HELP_AssignGlAccount.adoc-0].

How to set GL defaults and journals (practical points)
1. Put all common/tax-required accounts in the Global master so the Company can use them for consolidated reporting; add store‑level accounts (or store‑specific sub‑accounts) there as needed, then assign to store Organizations so each store can post to its own accounts while remaining under the master chart [HELP_ListGlAccountOrganization; HELP_AssignGlAccount] [doc:applications/accounting/src/docs/asciidoc/_include/HELP_ListGlAccountOrganization.adoc-0][doc:applications/accounting/src/docs/asciidoc/_include/HELP_AssignGlAccount.adoc-0].
2. Give each Organization its own Journals if you need separate posting streams or reconciliation per store (journals are supported per Organization) — otherwise keep journal use minimal and let automated postings drive entries [7766061-14].
3. For internal transfers, create and maintain inter‑org transfer/clearing accounts in the Global chart and assign them to the relevant Organizations so inventory transfers and inter‑store movements can be posted and reconciled per store and eliminated on consolidation [HELP_ListGlAccountOrganization] [doc:applications/accounting/src/docs/asciidoc/_include/HELP_ListGlAccountOrganization.adoc-0].
4. If you change any account (e.g., replace Inventory with a custom account), update the GL defaults and any references so automated postings continue to use the correct accounts [HELP_ListGlAccountOrganization] [doc:applications/accounting/src/docs/asciidoc/_include/HELP_ListGlAccountOrganization.adoc-0].

Operational tips
- Only assign the accounts each Organization actually needs (you can use a subset of the master template) to keep charts manageable and reporting clear [HELP_ListGlAccountOrganization] [doc:applications/accounting/src/docs/asciidoc/_include/HELP_ListGlAccountOrganization.adoc-0].
- Export Chart of Accounts details (CSV/PDF) to review mappings and to help tax/consolidation checks [HELP_ListGlAccountOrganization] [doc:applications/accounting/src/docs/asciidoc/_include/HELP_ListGlAccountOrganization.adoc-0].

References: acc-intro, master chart and assignment, and journals/organization support as cited above [doc:applications/accounting/src/docs/asciidoc/_include/acc-intro.adoc-0][doc:applications/accounting/src/docs/asciidoc/_include/HELP_ListGlAccountOrganization.adoc-0][doc:applications/accounting/src/docs/asciidoc/_include/HELP_AssignGlAccount.adoc-0][7766061-14].

These high‑level scenarios are a good start and align with the existing OFBiz sanity checklist items. Below are focused refinements and a few additional sanity checks to include, mapped to the OFBiz sanity test areas so they can be added to your document.

Suggested refinements / additions
- Include Order List validation as part of order entry checks: verify Print Pick Sheet, Contact Info, Payment Info, Shipment Info, Order Items, and Find Order functionality (use after Create Order) [71014328-2].
- Explicitly add Purchase Order entry coverage alongside Sales Order entry (your plan already matches the sanity checklist) [71014328-2].
- Add frontend cart/checkout sanity checks for Add-to-cart, cart quantities/prices, success messages, and checkout/order review (covers same flows for backend order creation validation) [71014328-0].
- Add Quote/Request-related checks where relevant to the sales flow: view quote page, quote roles/items/notes/attributes/prices and request creation/overview/roles/items (use when orders originate from quotes/requests) [71014328-2].
- Add fulfillment (warehouse) sanity tests tied to order fulfillment: create/manage picklist, print pick sheet, pack order, shipment processing and verify shipment information on the order (end‑to‑end from pick to ship) [71014328-3][71014328-2].
- Verify inventory effects after fulfillment: receiving inventory, inventory count, stock movement and manage variances where applicable (ensure stock changed by fulfillment) [71014328-3].
- Add Returns and post‑fulfillment checks (return initiation and processing) and include verification of related reports (order/fulfillment/returns reports) [71014328-2].
- Add explicit payment/state transition checks: verify payment info recorded, that orders created show expected initial status, and that status/approval flows differ by payment method (COD/Offline vs. processed Credit Card)—add tests for the Approve Order action and status change after payment processing [71014328-2].
- Add quick checks for order view/navigation after creation (unique Order ID, navigation to order view, order items and totals visible) — these are covered under Order Entry / Order List checks [71014328-2][71014328-0].

Recommended minimal checklist structure (for each sanity run)
- Create order: set product store/channel, select customer, add product(s), verify cart and success messages, set shipping/billing addresses, select shipping/payment, review totals, Create Order → verify Order ID and Order View [71014328-0][71014328-2].
- Order List/View checks: confirm contact/payment/shipment/items/print pick sheet/find order [71014328-2].
- Payment/status checks: verify approval options and status transitions per payment method [71014328-2].
- Fulfillment checks: create/print picklist, pack order, ship order, confirm inventory and shipment reflected on order [71014328-3][71014328-2].
- Post‑fulfillment: returns and reports verification [71014328-2][71014328-3].

What you describe is not a bug in your steps but a known hazard of running with the demo data and the Party Manager editing UI.

Key points from the docs:
- The Party Manager UI lets you open a party, click the User Name(s) form’s Edit button and change that user’s password (the docs use the admin example) — so the UI provides that capability from the party profile [170266058-36].  
- OFBiz demo data ships with an "admin" party and default passwords; running with demo data without changing those accounts is insecure [7045138-8].  
- The project explicitly warns: in production never use demo credentials and secure or disable those demo userlogins (admin, flexadmin, demoadmin, etc.) via the Party Manager — change passwords or disable accounts [7045142-1][61330745-0].  
- General security guidance: the preloaded user logins/permissions in demo data are potential back doors; secure your deployment per the How to secure your deployment guidance [48202125-1][7045142-1].

Recommended fixes (short):
- Immediately restore admin access: use a box/session where you still have an admin login (or restore from backup) and change admin’s password to a strong one and/or disable extra demo accounts via Party Manager [7045142-1][170266058-36].  
- Do not run with demo data on public systems; remove/replace demo data or load only your own seed/ext data as described in the production setup guide [7045138-8].  
- Audit and remove any unintended role/permission assignments for demo accounts and follow the "How to secure your deployment" checklist [7045142-1][48202125-1].

References: [170266058-36] [7045138-8] [7045142-1] [61330745-0] [48202125-1]

Short answer — use OFBiz’s tenant-id or tenant-specific domain to identify the tenant in the React app, let OFBiz route requests to the tenant’s database, and configure tenant-specific files in OFBiz. Key points and concrete steps:

1) Tenant identification between React and OFBiz
- Choose one of the supported methods:
  - Tenant ID in the login form (and include it in subsequent API calls), or
  - Tenant-specific domain/URL (React served on tenant domain; backend detects tenant from host) [14814279-1] [49579254-2].

2) Authentication flow
- Have the React frontend send the tenant identifier as part of the login request (or serve the React app on the tenant domain so OFBiz can infer the tenant). OFBiz uses the tenant identifier to pick the correct tenant data instance/database for the user session [14814279-1] [49579254-2].

3) Tenant data isolation and scaling
- OFBiz keeps each tenant’s data in a separate database (separate data instances) — design your deployment and database scaling around one DB per tenant. New tenant DBs can be added without restarting the server (self-service DB-driven model) [14814279-1] [49579254-1].

4) Frontend multitenancy support
- If you want the front store to be tenant-specific (tenant domain hosting the frontend), use OFBiz’s front-store multitenancy support so the front-end can be run on tenant-specific domain(s). OFBiz supports multiple domains per tenant and tenant-specific domain configuration [49579254-2] [49579254-1].

5) OFBiz configuration to enable multi-tenant behavior
- Ensure you add/adjust the tenant config files listed by OFBiz:
  - OFBIZ-HOME/framework/entity/data/<yourTenantConfig>.xml
  - OFBIZ-HOME/framework/entity/config/entityengine.xml
  - OFBIZ-HOME/framework/entity/ofbiz-component.xml
  Configure the tenant databases and components there so OFBiz will route to the correct database per tenant [14814279-3].

6) Practical recommendations (based on above)
- Detect tenant on the React side by host header or initial routing and include tenant identifier on all backend API calls.
- Prefer tenant-specific domains when you need per-tenant front stores and clearer separation; use tenant-ID form-based login when domains are not possible [49579254-2] [49579254-1].
- Keep tenant-specific configuration in the OFBiz tenant config files so OFBiz can select the proper DB/component at runtime [14814279-3].

If you want, tell me which tenant-identification method (tenant-id in form vs tenant domain) you prefer and I’ll outline the minimal changes you’ll need in the React app and the exact OFBiz config files to update.

Short answer — two ways:

1) Direct JDBC (edit inline-jdbc)
- Put the PostgreSQL JDBC driver JAR under framework/entity/lib/jdbc first [165223099-4].
- Edit the inline-jdbc element in framework/entity/config/entityengine.xml (example form shown in the docs). Replace the jdbc-uri value with your SSL-enabled JDBC URL (Postgres JDBC driver parameters go in the URL) and keep other attributes the same. Example form from the docs:
  <inline-jdbc jdbc-driver="org.postgresql.Driver" jdbc-uri="jdbc:postgresql://127.0.0.1:5433/ofbiz" jdbc-username="postgres" jdbc-password="postgres" isolation-level="ReadCommitted" pool-minsize="2" pool-maxsize="250" .../>
  (Change the jdbc-uri to your host/db and add the driver-specific SSL options) [71013152-12][6553994-2][165223099-4].

2) Avoid putting username/password in entityengine.xml (use JNDI)
- Configure a JNDI datasource in your app server with SSL and credentials, and then use the jndi-jdbc element in entityengine.xml so OFBiz uses the container datasource instead of inline credentials. The docs show this form (commented example):
  <jndi-jdbc jndi-server-name="default" jndi-name="java:comp/env/jdbc/localpostgres" isolation-level="ReadCommitted"/>
  Use that in place of inline-jdbc so you don't have to put username/password into entityengine.xml [71013152-12].

References: examples of inline-jdbc and jndi-jdbc and where to put JDBC drivers in OFBiz config: [71013152-12], [6553994-2], [165223099-4].

Short answer: Yes — your approach is the recommended pattern. Key points and caveats from the write-up:

What to do
- Use non‑sales types: model orders as FULFILLMENT_ORDER and shipments as FULFIL_SHIPMENT, and ensure FULFILLMENT_ORDER is standalone (not a child of SALES_ORDER) so sales ECAs don’t re‑attach [430409055-2][430409055-3].  
- Tenancy by stock/entities: one ProductStore per merchant (payToPartyId = merchant), ProductStoreFacility to link warehouse, ProductStoreRole for API clients, orders isolated by OrderHeader.productStoreId, and commingled inventory distinguished by InventoryItem.ownerPartyId = merchant [430409055-5].

Why this avoids order‑to‑cash
- Billing ECAs are gated on sales types; non‑sales order/shipment types prevent auto‑invoice / auto‑payment / GL posting from firing, so you get “zero order‑to‑cash” by construction [430409055-3].  
- The invoice ECA fires for any SALES_SHIPMENT and cannot be toggled off — so using a non‑sales shipment type is required to avoid accidental invoicing [430409055-1][430409055-3].

Operational caveats (you must implement extra logic)
- The standard high‑level shipping pipeline (quickShipEntireOrder / findOrdersToPickMove) is sales‑coupled and will not work for FULFILLMENT_ORDER; a FULFILLMENT_ORDER falls into the PO branch and won’t produce a usable shipment automatically [430409055-4].  
- You’ll need to drive lower‑level services in order: Receive (receiveInventoryProduct), Intake (storeOrder / approve), Reserve (reserveStoreInventory), Pick (observe reservation), Track (createShipmentRouteSegment), Ship (createShipment → issue items → updateShipment through PACKED → SHIPPED), and Poll readbacks [430409055-4].  
- OFBiz lacks a complete non‑sales “issue inventory to shipment” composite service — hand‑roll issuance with createItemIssuance + createInventoryItemDetail and set availableToPromiseDiff = 0 (reserve already lowered ATP) to avoid negative ATP [430409055-4].

Conclusion
- Your current design (non‑sales order/shipment types + ProductStore per merchant + InventoryItem.ownerPartyId for commingled stock) is exactly the recommended pattern, with the expected tradeoff that you must implement the non‑sales shipping/issuance flow yourself rather than reuse quickShipEntireOrder [430409055-5][430409055-2][430409055-4].

Short answer — two realistic ways, depending on whether your Docker image runs OFBiz with the embedded Derby DB or with another DB (Postgres/H2):

1) If OFBiz in the container uses embedded Derby
- Use an external Derby-aware client (Eclipse DTP or SQuirreL) and point it at the OFBiz runtime Derby database directory (example JDBC URL form: jdbc:derby:/path/to/ofbiz/runtime/data/derby/ofbiz) and use the OFBiz dev credentials (ofbiz/ofbiz) [6553844-47] [65865705-1].
- With Eclipse DTP: create a "Derby Embedded Database" connection, add the Derby JDBC driver (derby.jar) from your Gradle cache (Derby is provided at runtimeOnly in Gradle), set Database location to the OFBiz runtime/data/derby path, uncheck "Create database (if required)", then Test Connection [65865705-1] [65865705-2].

2) If the Docker image uses Postgres or embedded H2
- The Docker build/run supports switching to PostgreSQL vs embedded H2 via environment/config (see Docker build/run docs). Verify which DB your container is configured to use before trying to connect with a Derby client [7045138-9].

Notes / next steps
- Find the actual runtime path inside the container (usually runtime/data/derby/ofbiz) and either run the DB client inside the container or make that directory available to the client (so the Derby embedded driver can open the same DB files) — the client must use the file-path JDBC URL format above [6553844-47] [65865705-1].
- Test the connection in your client after configuring the driver and URL [65865705-2].

References: [65865705-1], [65865705-2], [6553844-47], [7045138-9]

Short answer / recommended approach

1) Acknowledge scope
- OFBiz includes a POS module and accounting features, but POS/batched aggregated imports and “sales without a Sales Order → full accounting” are not fully automatic out‑of‑the‑box [6553827-1]. 

2) Inventory (outgoing sales) — two approaches
- If you can: create real SALES_ORDER records and use OFBiz order→shipment flow (shipments become SALES_SHIPMENT when tied to SALES_ORDER). That keeps the standard pipeline and stock/accounting behavior [430409055-4].  
- If you cannot create a Sales Order for each aggregate (typical for aggregated POS batches): hand‑roll the inventory issuance because OFBiz has no complete non‑sales “issue inventory → shipment” one‑call service. Recommended actions (in this order): create or use a FULFILLMENT_ORDER if helpful, or directly call the lower‑level services to perform issuance:
  - use createItemIssuance + createInventoryItemDetail to record the physical issue, and when adjusting ATP ensure availableToPromiseDiff is handled (set availableToPromiseDiff = 0 if you already reserved to avoid double subtraction) [430409055-4].  
  - don’t expect to be able to jump directly to SHIPPED with the high‑level one‑call shipper; drive lower‑level services yourself as described [430409055-4].

3) Financial transactions / payments (cash, card)
- Represent bank/merchant accounts using Financial Accounts (FinAccount) and import statement lines into a common bank‑statement structure (one parser per bank format). Each statement line should be stored and later linked to accounting transactions and reconciled; implement a UI to match lines to transactions and create missing transaction items from a line when needed, with states like CREATED / RECONCILED [6553752-1].  
- You will likely need a parser/ingest job to turn POS payments into FinAccount/bank‑statement lines, and a reconcile/match UI to attach them to OFBiz payment/accounting records [6553752-1].

4) Accounting entries — custom glue needed
- Because OFBiz will not automatically generate the full set of GL postings for aggregated non‑order shipments/payments, implement custom services that:
  - when you record the item issuance, create the corresponding inventory/COGS and sales GL entries (credit inventory, debit COGS, credit sales revenue, debit FinAccount/cash as appropriate), and
  - when you import bank/merchant statements, create or match payment transactions and post GL entries so FinAccount and the GL stay in sync. The bank‑statement import / FinAccount → GL mirroring requires custom linkage (the docs note the need to mirror FinAccount transactions into GL so balances stay synchronized) [6553752-1].

5) Implementation checklist (minimal)
- Decide whether to create SALES_ORDER or use hand‑rolled issuance. If hand‑rolled, use createItemIssuance + createInventoryItemDetail and manage ATP adjustments [430409055-4].  
- Build POS batch importer/parsers that emit either Sales Orders or item issuance + payment records.  
- Use FinAccount and a bank‑statement table for storing imported payment lines; provide match/reconcile UI and states (CREATED/RECONCILED) [6553752-1].  
- Implement custom services to post required GL entries when ingesting POS sales and when reconciling payments so ledger and FinAccount remain consistent [6553752-1].

If you want, I can convert this into a concrete sequence of services and entities to call per POS batch (example service call order for hand‑rolled path), or sketch the DB structure/fields to store imported bank statement lines. Citations: POS/accounting feature note [6553827-1]; inventory/issuance guidance [430409055-4]; bank‑statement / FinAccount & reconciliation requirements [6553752-1].

2) Review the "Revisions Requiring Data Migration" page for a sequential list of version-to-version changes and any manual actions required. For Gradle-based releases (18.x+) the documented upgrade commands are:
   - svn up or git pull
   - ./gradlew clean
   - ./gradlew "ofbiz --load-data readers=seed"
   - ./gradlew ofbiz
   [7045166-0]

3) If you are coming from an older Ant-based workflow, the older (pre-Gradle) steps shown are:
   - svn up
   - ./ant clean
   - ./ant run-install-seed
   - ./startofbiz.sh
   Also follow the guidance to run the updated OFBiz on a non-public server so it can perform automatic DB table changes and the sequence of services between revisions [27828789-0].

4) Important notes:
   - The Revisions page explains the pattern for entity/field deprecations and automatic DB changes; follow its entries for any manual migration work between your current revision and 18.x [7045166-0][27828789-0].
   - Old data-migration services have been removed from trunk, so check the revisions list for any required unload/reload/convert activities before upgrading [7045166-0].

5) For hands-on learning about the target release, consult the OFBiz Tutorial for 18.12 (beginners’ development guide) [184617942-2].

A few related notes from the official docs:
- OFBiz is built as a suite of applications on a common architecture that makes components easy to customize and extend — a good fit for virtual/variant product models [93325429-1].  
- The applications support management of products and related processes, so designing flexible product models is in scope for OFBiz customizations [6553969-2].

Short answer: there’s no single published “maximum concurrent users” for OFBiz — it depends on customizations and load profile, and the docs explicitly recommend doing performance/load testing for your setup [6553844-92].

What the available docs show:
- Community installs tend to have small user bases (survey: 47% reported “10 or more” users, but the survey cutoff prevented larger detail) — many respondents are integrators rather than large end sites [47383011-9][47383011-3].  
- A rule‑of‑thumb from the docs: a decent mid‑range server (dual CPU, 4 GB RAM) can typically handle about 100,000 page hits per hour — how many concurrent users that corresponds to depends entirely on how often each user requests pages and what each request does [6553844-92].

Recommendation: run realistic load tests for your customisation and expected user behaviour to determine concurrent‑user capacity for your deployment [6553844-92].

Short answer: Yes — OFBiz ships a rest-api component that can expose services as REST endpoints out‑of‑the‑box [doc:framework/rest-api/src/docs/asciidoc/rest-api.adoc-0].

How to enable (summary from the docs)
- Use the rest-api component (location: framework/rest-api on trunk; plugin in ofbiz-plugins for older releases) [340037428-0].  
- Expose an existing service by setting export="true" in its service definition; once exported it is reachable at /rest/services/{service_name} and accepts GET, POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE. Parameter rules: for GET put a JSON object in the inParams query parameter; for POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE send a JSON body. Example curl shown in the docs [340037428-2].  
- Or define REST endpoints explicitly with a <component>.rest.xml placed in the component's api directory following rest-api.xsd. The XML maps resource paths and HTTP verbs to OFBiz services (example and element details shown in the docs) [340037428-4][doc:framework/rest-api/src/docs/asciidoc/rest-api.adoc-0].  
- Swagger UI for exposed APIs is available at: https://localhost:8443/docs/swagger-ui.html (per the rest-api docs) [340037428-5].

Notes
- The XML operation uses verb="get|post|put|patch|delete" (not action). Some newer attributes (customHeaders, primaryPermission, mainAction) exist on trunk but not in release24.09 [340037428-4].
